Summarize an Impact Analysis Result

Source: R/trace_impact_report.R
summarize_impact.Rd

Rolls up the per-variable result of trace_impact() into the digest a data team reads first: how many downstream variables are affected, broken down by dataset and by distance (level) from the change. The detailed result from trace_impact() lists every affected variable with its path; this condenses it to counts, and prints a short overview as a side effect.

Usage

summarize_impact(impact, ...)

Arguments

impact

A tibble returned by trace_impact(), with columns dataset, variable, role, depth, and path.

...

Ignored, for future extension.

Value

Invisibly, a list with two tibbles: by_dataset (one row per affected dataset with n_impacted, nearest_depth, farthest_depth) and by_level (one row per depth with n_impacted). A short summary is printed as a side effect. When nothing is impacted, both tibbles have zero rows.

Details

summarize_impact() does no graph work. It operates purely on the tibble returned by trace_impact(), reading the "changed" attribute to label the change. "Level" here is the depth column: the number of derivation hops between the changed variable and the affected one, so level 1 is a direct dependent and deeper levels are reached through a chain.

Examples

adam <- data.frame(
  dataset = c("ADSL", "ADAE", "ADTTE"), variable = c("AGE", "AAGE", "TAGE"),
  label = c("Age", "Analysis Age", "Time Age")
)
sdtm <- data.frame(dataset = "DM", variable = "AGE", label = "Age")
map <- data.frame(
  adam_dataset = "ADSL", adam_var = "AGE",
  sdtm_domain = "DM", sdtm_var = "AGE", confidence = 1
)
tm <- build_trace_model(adam, sdtm, mapping = map)
deriv <- data.frame(
  from_dataset = c("ADAE", "ADTTE"), from_var = c("AAGE", "TAGE"),
  to_dataset = c("ADSL", "ADAE"), to_var = c("AGE", "AAGE")
)
imp <- trace_impact(tm, "DM.AGE", adam_derivations = deriv)
rollup <- summarize_impact(imp)
#> ℹ Impact of changing "DM.AGE": 3 downstream variables affected.
#> ℹ   By dataset: ADAE (1), ADSL (1), and ADTTE (1)
#> ℹ   By level: L1 (1), L2 (1), and L3 (1)
rollup$by_dataset
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   dataset n_impacted nearest_depth farthest_depth
#>   <chr>        <int>         <int>          <int>
#> 1 ADAE             1             2              2
#> 2 ADSL             1             1              1
#> 3 ADTTE            1             3              3
